You have not done the work required at the test node: the report is only a (truncated) design plan, and no lru_cache.py or test_lru_cache.py exists in the working directory, so nothing has been implemented or verified. Complete the task: (1) implement lru_cache.py per the locked design — capacity<=0 raises ValueError, get-hit promotes MRU, LRU eviction on overflow, lazy TTL (expired get/has return miss without clearing; size() counts stored entries including lazily-expired ones, so size()<=capacity always holds), hits/misses/stats() with hit_rate=hits/(hits+misses) guarded for 0/0, and clear() that empties entries WITHOUT resetting stats (as instructed at the design node — do not silently flip this to resetting counters); (2) write test_lru_cache.py covering all requirements (TTL expiry, capacity boundaries, hit rate, and the 8-thread barrier-based concurrency tests for no-exceptions, size<=capacity, and no-lost-live-keys); (3) run `python3 -m pytest test_lru_cache.py -q` in the container until all pass; (4) report the exact 'N passed' summary and confirm the file locations. Your report also ends mid-sentence — submit a complete report.

You resubmitted the same truncated design draft; lru_cache.py and test_lru_cache.py still do not exist, and there is no pytest output or 'N passed' summary. Write the two files now (impl: dict + lock, del/reinsert for MRU, pop-first for LRU, lazy TTL via time.monotonic(), size() counting stored entries, hits()/misses()/stats() with 0/0-guarded hit_rate, clear() keeping stats, ValueError for capacity<=0; tests: capacity errors, LRU eviction + get-promotion, TTL expiry + lazy non-clearing, hit-rate, clear semantics, 8-thread barrier tests for no-exceptions/size<=capacity/no-lost-live-keys), run `python3 -m pytest test_lru_cache.py -q` until green, and reply with the exact 'N passed' line and file paths.
